sections.problem: In this fictional scenario, neighbors share tools through a volunteer-run lending library. Requests arrive in separate messages, so volunteers cannot tell which tool is available or whether two bookings overlap.
sections.users: Members who borrow tools and volunteers who manage the lending desk.
sections.outcomes: Members can see tool availability and request a booking. Volunteers can identify conflicts before confirming a loan. These are intended outcomes, not measured results.
sections.useCases:
UC-01: A member checks tool availability.
UC-02: A member requests or cancels a booking.
UC-03: A volunteer checks a tool back in.
sections.scope: One fictional lending location. Show tools, accept booking requests, prevent overlapping confirmed bookings, and record returns.
sections.nonGoals: Payments, delivery, identity checks, damage fees and connections to real inventory systems.
sections.inputsOutputs: Inputs: a selected tool, booking start and end, and the member action. Outputs: availability, a booking result, a clear error or a return status.

requirements.outcome: Members can identify a tool they may borrow.
requirements.behavior: Show each tool and whether it is available, booked or out of service.
requirements.acceptance: Each listed tool shows its name and current availability. An empty catalog shows a clear message.

requirements.outcome: Members can state when they need a tool.
requirements.behavior: Let a member request a tool for a start and end time.
requirements.acceptance: A request with an end time after its start can be submitted. An end time equal to or earlier than the start is rejected without creating a request.

requirements.outcome: Two members are not promised the same tool at the same time.
requirements.behavior: Prevent overlapping confirmed bookings for the same tool.
requirements.acceptance: A volunteer cannot confirm a booking that overlaps an existing confirmed booking for that tool. A booking that starts when another ends is allowed.

requirements.outcome: The next member sees the correct availability.
requirements.behavior: Let a volunteer record that a tool was returned and whether it needs maintenance.
requirements.acceptance: A returned tool becomes available when no booking or maintenance hold blocks it. A tool marked for maintenance remains unavailable.

requirements.outcome: Members can withdraw requests they no longer need.
requirements.behavior: Let a member cancel an unconfirmed booking request.
requirements.acceptance: Canceling an unconfirmed request removes it from the pending list. It does not change another member’s request or a confirmed booking.

requirements.outcome: Members can prepare to return a tool on time.
requirements.behavior: Offer an optional reminder before a tool is due back.
requirements.acceptance: Only members who opt in receive a reminder. Reminder timing and delivery method still need a decision before this requirement can be tested.

sections.quality: Booking and return actions must work with a keyboard and show clear validation errors. Display times in the lending location’s timezone. The timezone and performance targets are not documented.
sections.metrics: Proposed measures: conflicting confirmations and requests completed without volunteer help. Baselines, targets and measurement methods are not documented.
sections.risks: Pending requests may appear available while a volunteer is reviewing them. The team must agree whether a pending request holds a tool.
sections.decisions: Decide whether pending requests hold availability. Choose the lending timezone. Decide reminder timing and delivery method before including reminders in a release.
sections.evidence: This PRD is entirely fictional. Its review verdicts, proof and attachments are simulated examples. No real product, user research or test result is represented.
